The Chrome, webcam and voice paths need an Apple Silicon Mac with Chrome and were judged by reading.

reads.best: Tool-execution and model middleware let it change Hermes's execution semantics, with effect review, dependency checks and a substantial test suite.
reads.worst: Its large and intricate interception surface has unavoidable edge cases, especially when commands or unknown effects cannot be previewed.

reads.best: Tool middleware, effect ledgers, drift checks and fork comparison create a substantive new way to review agent actions.
reads.worst: Apply relies on non-interactive tool dispatch that auto-approves dangerous-command prompts, and live rehearsal state disappears on gateway restart.

reads.best: Extraordinarily thorough test suite (482 lines, plus Hermes-integration and opt-in real-CLI end-to-end tests) covering concurrent writers, fail-closed behavior, and approval codes cryptographically bound to the exact reviewed diff.
reads.worst: No screenshots or visual assets; the README itself admits editing the pin-store file directly (rather than a definition) is a gap the plugin does not catch.

reads.best: Covers eager tools and deferred discovery with fail-closed pin storage, definition-bound review codes and real-agent-loop integration tests.
reads.worst: It cannot catch server behavior changes without definition changes, trusts first use by default, and does not cover Codex app-server MCP calls.

reads.best: Extends where Hermes runs onto the user's own machine with no agent on the Mac, approval-gated and credential-file aware, with a demo and offline CI.
reads.worst: Requires macOS plus SSH key setup and cua-driver, and the tests are few for such a powerful tool.

reads.best: Keeps one agent and memory across two machines, with separate approval scopes, resolved-path gates, real remote timeouts and offline/live test harnesses. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vishnu-Aithal/hermes-remote-hands/f807ba317cc55ff8b6cbf7668f243f98fb9218b4/__init__.py
reads.worst: Mac setup is lengthy, the bypass guard is explicitly best effort, and screen integration depends on private Hermes internals and an externally installed driver. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vishnu-Aithal/hermes-remote-hands/f807ba317cc55ff8b6cbf7668f243f98fb9218b4/README.md

reads.best: Ambitious new capability with approval gating and owner-consented SMS OTP release, secrets declared via requires_env.
reads.worst: Very large codebase (~900KB) that is hard to review, and setup needs a paid Twilio account plus a tunnel; tests (~1,400) sit at the repo root outside the plugin folder.

reads.best: Scoped single-use consent, restricted per-call Hermes sessions and extensive call/OTP tests support a real phone capability on the user's own account.
reads.worst: Twilio, a public tunnel and a separate call profile make setup substantial, while live detection of a real agent and successful bridging remain unproven in the documented trials.

reads.best: Directly improves Hermes skill maintenance with revision-bound publication, source preservation, profile isolation and unusually thorough failure-recovery tests.
reads.worst: V1 excludes plugin-registered skill bundles and never switches a running conversation to the preferred derivative, limiting seamless adoption.

reads.best: Revision and review-hash checks, immutable snapshots, no-replace publication and fault/path-boundary tests make source-preserving customization unusually careful.
reads.worst: It does not switch the running session to the preferred derivative, cannot accept plugin-bundled sources, and textual merges still need human behavioral review.

reads.best: Its invariant-driven policy, hold ledger, timezone handling, owner approvals, reminders, fixture demo, and broad tests make a risky automation domain unusually careful.
reads.worst: The pinned release explicitly leaves the Google Workspace adapter unwired, so the impressive tested fixture path does not yet deliver the advertised real-calendar integration.

reads.best: It turns prior human decisions into durable, scoped agent context with unusually strong audit, Desktop, recovery, and safety disclosures.
reads.worst: The cooperative veto can leave a worker card running, and matching text is not proof that the ruling was actually applied.

reads.best: Durable ruling records, bounded veto history and a Desktop retirement interface make human decisions reusable across workers.
reads.worst: Default enforcement can leave a worker card running indefinitely after a veto, and matching and compliance rely on word overlap and text markers.

reads.best: Directly improves agents running on small personal hardware through enforceable resource controls and tests covering actual cgroup isolation and OOM handling.
reads.worst: Isolation is Linux/systemd-dependent and begins after process discovery, so early allocations and work performed by an external Docker daemon escape the memory cap.

reads.best: The spend guard enforces caps and approval before money moves.
reads.worst: Live PayPal money against an external service.

reads.best: Purely observer-based (8 lifecycle hooks, 'never written to: no tools, no middleware, no approval answers'), every hook fails open, no credentials or network calls at all, and ships a banner image and dashboard screenshot plus a Node-based UI smoke test under React 19.
reads.worst: It adds no new agent capability beyond observability — useful for operators but not something that changes what the agent itself can do (lower on 'beyond a prompt' than plugins that add real tools/providers).

reads.best: Changes how Desktop organizes sessions, with a Desktop plugin, dashboard tab, screenshots and a mobile client.
reads.worst: Checks are ad-hoc check_ scripts rather than a pytest suite; requires gateway restart.

reads.best: Local event sources, approval for arming rules, queued delivery and Desktop controls make Hermes useful between user messages.
reads.worst: Injection and delivery acknowledgement are separate operations, so a crash between them can replay an event despite the README's never-fires-twice claim.

reads.best: It is a deeply integrated and unusually polished Desktop companion that makes Hermes activity legible and personable.
reads.worst: The optional overlay expands the attack and portability surface with OS capture, process/window integration, and external Electron dependencies.

reads.best: A pre_tool_call hook blocks any send-like tool call unless the matching lead is already approved, and unconditionally blocks sends during any cron/unattended execution — a host-enforced guardrail no prompt or skill could replicate.
reads.worst: The core idea (lead-gen scanning and scoring) is a familiar SaaS pattern; the novelty is mostly in the enforcement plumbing rather than the lead-gen concept itself.

reads.best: Figure checks, ledger revalidation, exact-text approvals and extensive adversarial tests enforce safeguards a prompt cannot provide.
reads.worst: It needs manual CSV imports rather than live accounting integration, and its restricted financial prose still requires a person to catch semantic errors.

reads.best: Deep, honest engineering for debugging Hermes: wire capture beside the transcript, credential redaction, 0600 storage and about 229 Python tests plus browser tests.
reads.worst: Relies on fragile internals (frame inspection, a process-wide httpx patch, private Hermes imports), stores full conversation content by default, and its manifests still mention unshipped features.

reads.best: Capability-aware validation, durable dismissal rules and a careful Desktop setup turn agent suggestions into a usable personal workflow without automatically sending them.
reads.worst: A run can consume 70–80k tokens as disclosed, and capability discovery and duplicate checks depend partly on undocumented Hermes imports with fallbacks.

reads.best: It replaces Hermes's memory provider with portable memory the owner controls; the plugin never signs or mints, chain reads are keccak-checked, recalled text is labelled as data, and secrets are refused at capture.
reads.worst: It is tied to one vendor's wallet and chain, the agent key falls back to a 0600 file instead of Hermes's secret store when keyring is absent, install is a manual git clone and copy, and there are only 38 tests.

reads.best: Genuinely new: a register_platform adapter that puts Hermes on a moving vehicle, with keys read through get_scoped_secret, constant-time access-key checks with lockout, and about 170 tests.
reads.worst: Heavy, partly unverified setup: the README admits the locked-phone and Ride Summary paths are untested, the wake word needs a local Emscripten build, the README's ride_character tool is not registered, and the STT helper inherits the full environment.

reads.best: A runnable proof script reproduces the README's example output end-to-end, and the README candidly discloses an upstream Hermes gap it has to work around.
reads.worst: Value only materializes for users who already run cron jobs through Hermes, a narrower audience than a general-purpose plugin.

reads.best: Repairs are checked against actual cron incident or execution state and exposed through tools and a Desktop health view.
reads.worst: The agent can save arbitrary check-command argv through watchdog_runbooks and run it directly via repair, with no plugin-side human approval; calling these user-authored checks understates that reach.

reads.best: A genuinely new idea for multi-agent coding, built on pre/post tool-call and transform hooks, with the token read only through get_secret, a trusted-gateway rule so a cloned repo cannot redirect edits, and a large test suite.
reads.worst: Setup is long (npx gateway, paste a token, set an agent id, open both sessions first), it serves only people running several coding agents on one repo, and the hosted option sends edit diffs off the machine.

reads.best: Automatic baseline capture, test overlay, tamper checks, and completion hooks directly improve coding-agent verification.
reads.worst: Test-runner recognition is an unanchored regex, and shell metacharacters trigger shell execution from tools or hooks without a separate approval gate.

reads.best: A shared revisioned evidence store and interactive Desktop workspace preserve citations and follow-up research beyond a chat response.
reads.worst: Claim extraction and verification depend on heuristics or the host model; direct ingestion accepts only bounded uncompressed RSS/Atom feeds, and social connectors remain future work.

reads.best: A polished, screenshot-documented Desktop product turns Hermes's own Kanban data into useful live and historical views while opening every board database read-only.
reads.worst: It serves Hermes Kanban users only, has no agent tools or model interaction, and requires separately enabling both the plugin and Desktop page.

reads.best: Combines object verification, deterministic term checks and visual evidence, reserving Meta-call costs before spending and escalating ambiguous object matches to a person.
reads.worst: Unreadable vision-tracking batches are counted as not seen, so a partial model failure can produce a definite contract-term FAIL instead of an unknown result.

reads.best: A new idea that only hooks can do: it measures the user's own agent's honesty and feeds the record back to make it check before claiming, using local pattern matching with no model calls.
reads.worst: Claim and outcome detection is regex pattern matching, so a vague next user message or an untested claim can be scored wrongly or left unchecked, and the README has no screenshot or demo.

reads.best: Finished product with a Desktop UI, print pipeline, CI and a deep Python and JS test suite.
reads.worst: Reliant on Google News RSS personal-use terms, and its optional model key is read from an env var.

reads.best: Layered limits (onchain scope and caps, plugin-side plan encoding, Hermes approval) with withdrawals only via Desktop plus WebAuthn, honestly disclosed, 48 tests and a full Desktop pane.
reads.worst: One 'Always' approval covers every later batch for that pool or swap pair regardless of amount (rule key ignores size), with slippage up to 5000 bps or a zero minAmountOut, so trades can move value without per-transaction approval.

reads.best: About 4,300 lines of engine code with 260 tests, model access only through Hermes's plugin LLM facade, friendly provider-error messages and a 2,800-line Desktop pane.
reads.worst: A niche decision-review tool whose 27,000-character README and committed internal notes (HANDOFF, SESSION-PROMPT, PROGRESS) promise more rigor (Shapley-priced objections, calibration) than a hundred-call LLM debate can deliver, and the PR is still unmerged.

reads.best: Turns one-off generated apps into persistent, agent-accessible tools with independent data, reversible code changes, and live updates from any chat platform.
reads.worst: Its CSP injection matches <header> and commented or late <head> tags, so generated app code can run before the promised network restriction is active.

reads.best: Deterministic calculations, a finished Desktop panel and extensive credential, timeout and data-edge tests make a strong personal-data integration.
reads.worst: Its audience needs a Garmin account and compatible device, and health interpretation remains dependent on wrist-sensor estimates and Garmin’s service.

reads.best: Fails closed when it errors, is honest that it is not an OS sandbox, and ships about 117 Python plus 53 frontend tests, screenshots and thorough docs.
reads.worst: The Control Room is a separate local web server rather than a Desktop pane, shell-command checks are allowlist word-splitting that can be bypassed, and restore only covers write_file/patch under a single-directory mission.

reads.best: The complete recording-to-reel workflow combines OBS control, persistent marks, native Desktop controls and substantive protocol, media and recovery tests.
reads.worst: Browser sources accept unchecked URLs and local or model-written HTML, while approval for source/design changes only fires during streaming, allowing unapproved local-page execution and private-network reads ([core/studio.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/perfect7613/hermes-onair/2245b9158300f2a60a5dda859f037b3cc3244b03/core/studio.py), [core/guard.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/perfect7613/hermes-onair/2245b9158300f2a60a5dda859f037b3cc3244b03/core/guard.py)).

reads.best: A polished and novel agent/robotics demo with real-policy simulation, a human-clearable e-stop, a fail-closed motion interlock, screenshots, and focused tests.
reads.worst: It is simulation-only, while its full backend requires a separately installed simulator and downloaded assets.

reads.best: Provides extensive physical-device capabilities, phone-side capability gates, human approval for selected risky tools, and regression tests that reject gated macro steps.
reads.worst: The shipped android_relay.py loads ANDROID_AGENT_TOKEN_* credentials from relay-config.json rather than Hermes secrets; setup docs also mix stale tool counts and German instructions.

reads.best: A durable per-tool ledger and native execution middleware target the important ambiguity between a side effect and its recorded result.
reads.worst: core.py marks an operation recovered whenever any fingerprinted target changed, so a partial or unrelated write can be mistaken for full completion despite the exactly-once claims.

reads.best: It materially improves unattended Hermes work with deterministic approval cards, owner checks, expiry, replay protection and focused adversarial tests.
reads.worst: Its --local filter-driver check misses included Git config before host-side git status, allowing repo-controlled filters to execute outside the agent sandbox; see [pinned drift code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xkinno/abeyance/4e8ddabfa8e2a000418df97886ed58d1f9257a0b/abeyance/drift.py).

reads.best: The actual memory-provider lifecycle preserves exact words across sessions and connects graph concepts back to their originating turns without a network service.
reads.worst: Graph validation and append are not one locked transaction, transcript books are written separately, and retrieval repeatedly loads whole growing files despite paginated output.

reads.best: Fresh approval keys, a minimal child environment, read-only role rules, verdict downgrades, and regression tests go well beyond a delegation prompt.
reads.worst: The do role bypasses Antigravity permissions after approval, while read-only checks are not OS isolation and miss ignored or already-untracked file edits.

reads.best: Lifecycle hooks, bounded draining, process-tree cleanup, scoped credentials and restricted child environments make idle hardware sharing more than a skill.
reads.worst: Setup needs a separate IE environment, model and llama-server, while tests use mock inference and production GPU behavior and alpha coordinator availability remain unverified.

reads.best: It integrates the real model picker with sourced comparison data, an offline fallback and explicit confirmation for guarded model switches. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer/4b876bb5021c56fe14e14a15d4e379b5e6506c9e/desktop/plugin.js)
reads.worst: Measured speed and spend are aggregated by normalized model ID without separating providers, so one provider's measurements can affect another's comparison. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer/4b876bb5021c56fe14e14a15d4e379b5e6506c9e/desktop/plugin.js)

reads.best: The implemented multi-process audio pipeline, hardware-aware setup, model routing, and finished companion UI substantially extend local hardware use. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestWaters/hermes-live-translator/315085f89fc675b119e1a412ef38873c1365c6da/README.md)
reads.worst: The loopback server serves its control token without validating Host and compares Origin to the supplied Host, leaving DNS-rebinding protection incomplete; real-time performance was not exercised in this read-only review. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestWaters/hermes-live-translator/315085f89fc675b119e1a412ef38873c1365c6da/live_translate/server.py)

reads.best: A real platform adapter with 17,000 lines, 154 tests, a security policy and documented recovery paths, and sign-in handled by Hermes rather than a key file.
reads.worst: The README says this catalog build needs an unmerged Hermes PR (#151209) and that stock Hermes users should install a different version from main, it is Linux-only, and the dense 27,000-character README makes setup hard to follow.

reads.best: Public result-transform and compaction hooks implement deterministic deduplication with fail-open behavior, a streak guard and focused tests.
reads.worst: The recall handler falls back from a failed session-scoped lookup to an unrestricted lookup, allowing a known result ID from another session to retrieve its stored output.

reads.best: The visual is unusually honest for a dashboard: it uses host state, avoids fabricated metrics and network access, and has a stable seeded field.
reads.worst: It is a narrow visualization with no agent tools, tests, or README setup beyond enabling the pane, so relatively few users need it on day one.

reads.best: Real cryptography and process isolation (separate system user, peer-uid socket checks, hardened systemd unit) with 83 tests across Python versions in CI.
reads.worst: It claims more than the code does. In default mode the password lands in a browser whose DevTools port is shared with the agent's browser tools, and the repo's own test reads it back from the field. Setup also needs root and a running daemon.

reads.best: A substantial game UI, opt-in networking and autonomy, and extensive client/server tests make this more than a pet-themed prompt.
reads.worst: The online client reads, writes and refreshes access and refresh tokens in its own session.json rather than using Hermes’s secret routes, contrary to catalog rule 11.

reads.best: Centralized consume authorization, persistent request IDs, readback confirmation and extensive failure-path tests support a polished account-wide rescue workflow.
reads.worst: It depends on undocumented ChatGPT mutation endpoints and explicitly deviates from catalog credential routing by handling pool tokens directly; automatic irreversible redemption is enabled by default.

reads.best: A substantial local-radio product has integration tests, illustrated setup and code-level restrictions reserving public broadcasting for a human command.
reads.worst: Its child adapter reads the station’s control.token file instead of obtaining credentials through Hermes, and a separate running station is required.

reads.best: New users get integrated setup cards, model-error fallbacks, secret-pattern checks and narrowly allowlisted import commands behind explicit clicks.
reads.worst: It is explicitly unfinished, has no shipped screenshots or videos, and its README opens by claiming it never installs or changes settings before disclosing importer and plugin-install actions.

reads.best: It intervenes before the model sees tool output, preserves JSON structure, and tests rule parity and metadata-only logging. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plutoskiz/herms-gate/26b6f797cd3fb3a4f1669953060d6ea3317ac04e/gate.py)
reads.worst: Fixed patterns can miss encoded or rephrased attacks and alter legitimate quoted text; on Hermes 0.21.5 hidden-message blocking falls back to a model-facing note. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plutoskiz/herms-gate/26b6f797cd3fb3a4f1669953060d6ea3317ac04e/README.md)

reads.best: Highly original and very polished, with images, clips, PDFs and about 370 tests.
reads.worst: Intrusive for a toy: pre_llm_call injects text telling the agent to relay its card verbatim, a polling thread starts at import in every process, and it reads parent processes' /proc environ.

reads.best: It gives Hermes a provider path to a broad catalog of open-weight models with no extra dependency.
reads.worst: It is a thin provider adapter with modest local surface area, limited documentation evidence beyond the README and no distinctive agent behavior.

reads.best: Finished like a product: banner, three screenshots, status-bar popover, command-palette actions and settings page, with no network, backend or secrets.
reads.worst: Cosmetic only: it does nothing for the agent, and its testing is a single end-to-end Desktop script.

reads.best: It uses the native prefetch and sync_turn lifecycle with profile-specific storage and scoped secrets, so recall happens automatically before a turn.
reads.worst: Notion sync stores only each page title as both title and body, while retrieval is substring matching rather than meaningful page-content memory.

reads.best: The Desktop-to-composer workflow turns spatial feedback into a persistent, structured revision brief with board ownership checks. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peterpeeterspeter/hermes-creative-review/3f09cdce305c9c9db19ce9d752134ca1a35344e0/README.md)
reads.worst: The central live Electron review-to-generation handoff remains unverified, with screenshots and a demo recording still pending. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peterpeeterspeter/hermes-creative-review/3f09cdce305c9c9db19ce9d752134ca1a35344e0/README.md)

reads.best: A coherent set of six formats, escaped HTML compilation, Markdown fallbacks and a finished Desktop guide make the presentation useful.
reads.worst: Most of the decision discipline is a bundled prompt contract; the code checks structure and wording rather than whether evidence or recommendations are sound.

reads.best: Authenticated loopback transport, bounded responses, device identity checks and Android-owned action confirmation are supported by extensive defensive test code.
reads.worst: The pinned preview reads and stores pairing credentials in files contrary to the catalog rule, omits Android build prerequisites, and has no verified end-to-end spoken conversation.

reads.best: Handles Sarvam specifics (reasoning_effort mapping, 16384 max tokens, filtering non-chat models) in a tiny clear profile with tests.
reads.worst: A ~60-line provider profile; niche audience and a common kind of plugin.

reads.best: Production code implements paced synthesis retries and speaker-aware mixing, and an ffprobe-based test checks the actual mastered audio metadata and chapters.
reads.worst: Speech depends on Microsoft Edge online TTS, and without ffmpeg the fallback loses mastering, pauses and embedded chapters; there is no Desktop production interface.

reads.best: A genuinely original use of an agent with a large readable toolkit (emulator driver, map/music/dialogue tools, BPS patch sharing), no ROM shipped, and loopback/Host/Origin gates on its local servers with tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes plugin itself registers zero tools and zero hooks, the README's own "Not tested yet" section lists the pane inside Desktop and the skill loaded through the plugin, and setup needs a heavy Linux-only toolchain.

reads.best: Hash-bound candidates, explicit unsupported-capability reports and regression tests make migration losses visible and repairs reviewable.
reads.worst: The guided workflow remains limited to a pinned pilot and disposable homes, while model-facing staging accepts a model-supplied approval flag for unsandboxed foreign-code inspection.

reads.best: Transaction-backed reservations, stable action identity and crash-recovery tests demonstrate a credible execution-and-learning loop across tools and dashboard.
reads.worst: All business data and ERP actions are synthetic; no production connector or company RBAC makes this usable for a real manufacturer yet.

reads.best: User-only approval commands, on-chain delegated spending caps and tested rule logic make the automation concrete.
reads.worst: The spending helper key is generated and read from helper.json rather than Hermes secret storage, contrary to the stated catalog credential rule.

reads.best: Read-only Desktop panes with tool-backed panel notes and widgets, two test files and graceful empty states when no notes vault is set.
reads.worst: Most useful to people running several bot profiles with an Obsidian-style vault, and the dev deploy.sh copies itself into every profile by poking install venvs.

reads.best: A native pre-tool approval hook makes production policy enforceable beyond a prompt, and credentials use Hermes secret scope.
reads.worst: It defaults to ungated dev mode even with live credentials, and interpolates unchecked model/method strings into request URLs rather than validating that the executed endpoint matches the gate decision.

reads.best: Model-specific payload validation, multiplex-safe secret access and tests for uploads, discovery and timeout cancellation make the API integration careful.
reads.worst: No live FAL generation is demonstrated, and the local-upload guard checks filename extensions and size rather than actual media content.

reads.best: Detailed production templates, worked examples and text-checking helpers support a coherent writing-to-video workflow.
reads.worst: The actual generation tools are hosted outside the pinned code, and no automated test suite verifies the connector or its paid production workflow.

reads.best: Uses the native provider profile instead of ad hoc HTTP tools, leaving key handling and request transport to Hermes.
reads.worst: There are no tests in the pinned repository, and auxiliary calls fail unless users manually configure the streaming-only endpoint workaround.

reads.best: Its live tools stop at drafts and track the thread's workflow in a profile-local SQLite ledger.
reads.worst: The claimed send gate trusts an `approved` field supplied in tool arguments, allowing a send-shaped call to bypass the allowlist and approval directive.

reads.best: The game UI and checksum-verified WAD backend are real, with safeguards against symlinked or blocking files.
reads.worst: It does little for the agent's work, and the tests cover the backend but not the browser game engine.

reads.best: It presents a clear, attractive niche creative workflow and correctly declares its authenticated remote server as untrusted in Hermes.
reads.worst: The reviewed commit is a thin hosted-service connector with no implementation or tests for its remote rendering and sharing behaviour.

reads.best: The capsule preserves goals, completed work, next steps and refuted approaches, with clear private-identity and untrusted-handoff guidance.
reads.worst: The Hermes package is chiefly a hosted MCP connector and ritual skill: its guardian hooks do not run in Hermes, and remote storage/recovery behavior is outside the pinned code.

reads.best: The package declares an untrusted server and a Hermes secret field, with explicit review and publishing guidance.
reads.worst: The marketing implementation is not in the pinned package, and its test report explicitly leaves the signed-in Hermes tool-call workflow incomplete.

reads.best: Clear README, OAuth instead of keys, untrusted trust level so spending and sending asks first.
reads.worst: No code, just a wrapper for a paid hosted service a skill plus MCP config could do.

reads.best: Server discovery followed by a single forwarded tool call can expand the agent’s reach without a separate install for each service.
reads.worst: The pinned package is configuration and a skill with no forwarding implementation or tests; its safety guarantees depend on a mutable hosted server.

reads.best: The backing service implements persistent SQLite and filesystem document storage, versioning and context retrieval beyond a prompt.
reads.worst: No test suite is present in the pinned tree, the Hermes README documents long-body tool-call failures, and the runtime licence resolver can read the sibling LoreConvo licence store outside Hermes’s secret routes.

reads.best: A minimal Hermes-specific README gives an explicit OAuth setup command and discloses that service queries are recorded. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thott-bot/plugin/af8439ac4c4560aba5303ee7578d921a33c7b5da/hermes/README.md)
reads.worst: Only connector manifests and documentation are pinned, with no server source or tests to substantiate freshness or coverage, and no documented opt-in for query recording. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thott-bot/plugin/af8439ac4c4560aba5303ee7578d921a33c7b5da/hermes/README.md)

reads.best: The wrapper uses argument lists, subprocess timeouts, a minimal child environment, and a default-off session-start pull.
reads.worst: The documented proof workflow passes --hypothesis to scout prove, but the Scout revision named by the plugin accepts only an ID there and exposes hypothesis as a separate subcommand; no plugin tests catch this mismatch.
